context_requirements: Cells must have an active sterol regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP) pathway to mount the compensatory transcriptional response.
Cells must express CYP51A1 and depend on de novo sterol synthesis for membrane and lipid homeostasis.
The drug must engage CYP51A1 at 10 micromolar; cells with high efflux or low intracellular accumulation may show weak responses.
falsifiers: No increase in SREBP target genes such as HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1, or INSIG1 at 6 h or 24 h in any cell line.
A decrease rather than an increase in SREBP target genes after treatment.
No change in any landmark gene across all nine cell lines at both time points.
A strong generic stress or apoptosis signature without the expected sterol-pathway transcriptional response.

changes: Removed EBP and NSDHL from proximal_up and late_up: these are downstream sterol biosynthesis enzymes, not established SREBP transcriptional targets; their inhibition is post-transcriptional and would not cause compensatory upregulation.
Removed ACAT2 from proximal_up and late_up: ACAT2 is not a canonical SREBP target and its direction under CYP51A1 inhibition is not justified.
Removed SCP2 from proximal_up and late_up: SCP2 is not a canonical SREBP target and its direction under CYP51A1 inhibition is not justified.
Kept HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1, and INSIG1 as SREBP target genes expected to increase after sterol depletion; no direction changes needed.
No generic proliferation or stress genes were present in the proximal lists, so no specificity removals were required.
No line-specific contradictions were identified; HEPG2 strong response is consistent with active hepatic sterol synthesis, and other lines remain moderate.
Kinetics and magnitude are consistent with SREBP-mediated transcriptional compensation: fast induction at 6 h and sustained moderate response at 24 h.
Evidence list is empty; no citations to validate.
